record.paper_title: New results and open questions for SIR-PH epidemic models with linear birth rate, loss of immunity, vaccination, and disease and vaccination fatalities
record.context_brief: Extension of the endemic/disease-free determinant formula to SIR-PH models
record.original_question: For SIR-PH models with linear birth rate, loss of immunity, vaccination, and disease-induced mortality, can the determinant identity Det(J_ee)=-Det(J_dfe), established for lower-dimensional SAIR first-approximation cases, be extended by exploiting the block partition of the scaled-model Jacobian into the susceptible coordinate and disease-coordinate block?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an SIR-PH compartmental epidemic model with phase-type-distributed infectious period, linear (constant-rate) birth, loss of immunity, vaccination, and disease-induced mortality. The state is partitioned into a scalar susceptible coordinate s and a vector of "disease" coordinates i (comprising the infectious phases and possibly removed/vaccinated compartments). After non-dimensional scaling, the model has two equilibria: a disease-free equilibrium (DFE) and an endemic equilibrium (EE), and an associated basic reproduction number R0. Let J_dfe and J_ee denote the Jacobians of the scaled vector field at the DFE and EE, respectively, and write each Jacobian in block form according to the partition into the susceptible coordinate and the disease-coordinate block.

For low-dimensional SAIR (susceptible–asymptomatic–infectious–removed) first-approximation models with no disease-induced mortality (δ=0), the following identity is known:
   Det(J_ee) = Λ v0 v1 v2 (1 − R0) = − Det(J_dfe),
where Λ is the birth rate and v0, v1, v2 are explicit coefficients arising from the model parameters.

Problem. Determine whether this determinant identity Det(J_ee) = − Det(J_dfe) extends to general SIR-PH models with linear birth rate, loss of immunity, vaccination, and disease-induced mortality, by exploiting the susceptible/disease block partition of the scaled-model Jacobian. If so, provide a general proof and an explicit formula for the common value of ±Det(J_ee) in terms of the model parameters and R0; otherwise, identify the obstructions and characterize the subclass of SIR-PH models for which the identity does hold.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted search did not surface a published proof or refutation extending the determinant identity Det(J_ee) = −Det(J_dfe) from the SAIR first-approximation case to general SIR-PH models with vaccination and disease-induced mortality. The question appears to remain an open research direction; status is recorded as unknown.

status_evidence.claim: The determinant identity extension is stated as an open problem rather than a theorem.
